venue.name: Filberg Heritage Lodge and Park
venue.description: Filberg Park is a nine acre waterfront property on Comox Harbour, owned by the Town of Comox and operated by the non profit Filberg Heritage Lodge and Park Association. The landscaped grounds are open year round from dawn until dusk with free admission, and contain rare and exotic trees, a stream, flowerbeds and open meadows. The 1930s Filberg Lodge on the site is a municipal heritage building that houses a volunteer run gift shop and opens for drop in tours on Thursdays over the summer. The Hands On Farm, a seasonal petting farm run through the Comox Recreation Centre, operates in the park in summer and takes bookings from schools, daycares and other groups.

facility_notes.washrooms: Filberg Park has two sets of washrooms that are available for use. Two are located by the Cutting Garden in the Boathouse, and two are located by the Grape Arbour. All of our washrooms are accessible and have a concrete path leading up to them. There is a changing table in the women's washroom located by the Grape Arbour. The Upper Washrooms will be open daily from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. After 4:00 PM, the Lower Washrooms, located by the beachfront by the Cutting Garden, will remain available for public use.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Meandering the paths and open meadows are perfect for a stroll, a picnic, or quiet contemplation.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Filberg Park has no control over the weather and does not have interior space available for use if it rains. Two 10 x 10 tents can be rented and require notice in advance to ensure that we have staff available to set them up.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: All of our washrooms are accessible and have a concrete path leading up to them. Filberg Park has three accessible parking spots in the driveway located by the Filberg Lodge.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Filberg Park has three accessible parking spots in the driveway located by the Filberg Lodge. All other guests will need to park along Comox Avenue and Filberg Road. Absolutely no parking on the driveway of Filberg Park.

restrictions: We do not allow any dogs or pets in the Park with the exception of certified assistant dogs
There is no smoking of any kind allowed on the Filberg Park grounds
venue.hours_notes: The Park is open daily from Dawn until Dusk (free admission). Gate 3 (Driveway Gate off Filberg Road) and Gate 2 (Off Filberg Road) are open daily from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. After 4:00 PM, use the pedestrian gate off Comox Avenue to enter and exit the park. The Filberg Lodge Administration Office is open Monday to Friday from 9 am to 3 pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: Lodge Tours run May 28 to August 27, every Thursday from 12 PM to 3 PM, no appointment needed. The Hands On Farm 2026 season ran 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, 7 days per week, June 8 to August 16, with a stated closure July 27 to August for the Filberg Festival. The Gift Shop is open Friday to Sunday from 11 am to 4 pm.

programs.name: Self-guided park and garden visit
programs.description: Free, year round access to the nine acre grounds and gardens, open daily from dawn until dusk. The park holds a herb garden, pollinator and butterfly beds, a bat box, mason bee houses, a green roof on the pump house and the Greig rhododendron collection. The Town of Comox and the association publish a free self-guided walk, The Trees of Filberg, as a downloadable guide divided into six sections so a visit can be broken up. No booking route, group rate or group size limit is published for ordinary park use.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the paths and open meadows between flowerbeds and rare trees, follow the printed tree walk from marker to marker, and look for the bat box on the fence line by Gate 1 and the mason bee houses around the grounds. There is a stream, a beachfront and open lawn to picnic on.
programs.our_note: This is the part of Filberg you can rely on year round, because the grounds are free and never close while the lodge and the farm only open in summer. There is nowhere indoors to shelter, so a wet forecast means a wet trip. Dogs are not allowed at all, which catches some families out.
programs.practical_summary: Free to walk in, washrooms in two places on site with a changing table in one, and picnicking on the meadows. There is no indoor room if it rains, and bus parking is not stated anywhere, so check before you bring a coach.
programs.evidence: Open year-round, the landscaped grounds contain rare and exotic trees, a stream and numerous flowerbeds.

programs.name: Hands On Farm group visit
programs.description: A seasonal petting farm inside Filberg Park, described on the park's own site but run through the Comox Recreation Centre. Schools, daycares and other groups book a time by phone or email, adults 18 and over come free with a group, and group rates apply. The rates themselves are not on the park's site, which sends visitors to the Town of Comox page for admission prices. Cash, debit and credit cards are accepted on site. The 2026 season ran 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, 7 days per week, from June 8 to August 16, with a stated closure from July 27 for the Filberg Festival.
programs.what_children_do: Walk into the barnyard to meet and talk to the farm animals up close, then stroll the park gardens or the lodge afterwards.
programs.our_note: This is the one thing at Filberg that is set up for a booked group, but it only runs for about ten weeks in summer and the price is not on the park's own site, so budget by phone before you commit. The farm is not run by the park association, so the number to call is a different one from the lodge office. The season dates on their page also do not quite line up with the festival closure they mention, which is worth pinning down when you call.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors, with washrooms and picnicking on the grounds nearby, and adults 18 and over free with a group. Price, minimum age, group size and how much notice they need are all unstated, so the booking call has to cover them.
programs.extra_fees_note: Adults (18 years and older) with groups are free. Group rates apply. Admission prices are not published on the park's own site; it links out to the Town of Comox for them.
programs.evidence: Bring your school, daycare or group to Hands on Farm.

programs.name: Filberg Lodge drop-in tour
programs.description: Volunteer guides show visitors through the 1930s Filberg Lodge, a 4,000 square foot Arts and Crafts style heritage house, and tell the stories of the home. The lodge also holds Bob's Office, a restored room about hand logging in the Comox Valley in the 1920s and 1930s with artifacts and photographs, and the volunteer run gift shop occupies the rooms of the house. Tours run May 28 to August 27, every Thursday from 12 PM to 3 PM, with no appointment needed. The site does not say what year those dates belong to and gives no price for the tour.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the rooms of an old wooden house with a guide, look at the leaded glass windows and stonework, and see the logging photographs and objects set out in Bob's Office.
programs.our_note: It is a drop in, not a booking, so a group turns up on a Thursday afternoon and takes its chances on how busy the house is. The rooms are full of china and glass laid out for sale, which is a lot of breakable things at toddler height. Ask whether they can take a whole class before you build a morning around it.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, one afternoon a week in summer only, with washrooms out in the park rather than in the house. No price, no group booking route and no group size limit are published, so ring the lodge office first.
programs.evidence: Step inside the historic Filberg Lodge from May 28 – August 27, every Thursday from 12 PM – 3 PM.

images.alt: A shingled wooden house with a steep gabled roof and leaded glass windows, seen across a flagstone path and a bed of pink and white flowers, with tall trees behind.
Six sheep and a black and white goat feeding on hay from a blue plastic trough on dry grass.
An open-sided timber stage with a pitched roof standing on a lawn, with picnic tables underneath and evergreens behind.
A round table in a wood-panelled room laid with green cloth, china place settings and cutlery, with a curtained leaded window and a display cabinet behind.

gaps: price: the Hands On Farm group rate is not published on filberg.com. The page says only 'Group rates apply' and links to the Town of Comox page for admission prices, which is off this venue's own domain and was not used as a source. A whole class fee could be anything, so ask on the booking call.
price: no price is published for the Filberg Lodge drop-in tour, so whether it is free is unknown rather than free.

youngest age: no minimum age is published for any offering here. The Hands On Farm page says only 'children of all ages', which is not a number, so the age fields are left blank. The one age figure on the site, 13 and over, is the minimum for farm volunteers, not visitors.
capacity: no group size limit is published for the farm, the lodge tour or the park.
lead time: no notice period is published for booking a Hands On Farm group time.

season already passed: the Hands On Farm 2026 season is given as June 8 to August 16, which has ended by the date of this check. The Lodge Tour season is given as May 28 to August 27 with no year attached, and it has also passed if 2026 was meant. Confirm the next season's dates before planning around either.

season dates unclear: the Hands On Farm page gives the season as June 8 to August 16 and in the next line says 'we'll be closed July 27 – August for the Filberg Festival', which does not fit inside that season. Worth settling on the booking call.

operator: the Hands On Farm is described on filberg.com but 'is run through the Comox Recreation Centre', and it uses a different phone number and email from the lodge. Bookings and prices are handled by the Town of Comox, not by the park association.
rain backup: the park states plainly that there is no interior space available if it rains, and the only covered options mentioned are two rentable 10 by 10 tents and the seasonal patio restaurant.

bus parking: not stated. The site only describes three accessible parking spots by the lodge and street parking on Comox Avenue and Filberg Road, with no parking allowed on the driveway. Whether a school bus can drop off and where is unpublished.

wheelchair and stroller access: the site says the washrooms are accessible with concrete paths, and that there are three accessible parking spots, but it does not say whether the grounds or the paths themselves are step free, so those fields are blank rather than yes.
months for the self-guided park visit are recorded as year round on the strength of 'Open year-round' on the grounds page.

coordinates: the site publishes no map pin, no map embed and no coordinates on any page opened. The point recorded was geocoded from the published street address and lands on the lodge building. For a nine acre park with several gates, that is the lodge rather than the gate you will drive to, so follow their gate instructions rather than the pin.

images: the home page serves its banner photographs as CSS background images rather than picture tags, and there is no Open Graph image on the home page, so the hero was taken from the home page banner. Every photograph used either has an empty alt attribute or a file name in place of one, so all four alt lines here were written by us after opening each image and looking at it.
the lodge is not open to visitors outside the summer Thursday tour window and the Friday to Sunday gift shop hours, so a winter or spring group visit is grounds only.

values: Friday to Sunday from 11 am to 4 pm
conflicts.note: Their gift shop page gives the days the lodge is open two different ways. One line says Friday to Sunday, another says weekends. If you want the house open when you arrive, check the day with them first.

values: no interior space available for use if it rains
heated covered patio with blankets and cozy indoor seating available
conflicts.note: One of their pages says there is nowhere indoors to go if it rains. Another says the restaurant in the park has a heated covered patio and some indoor seating. Ask whether a group can sit there in bad weather, because the two answers do not match.
